## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

+# Contentful Developer Guide
+
+A draft guide for working with Contentful on the Zimmermann PWA.
+
+---
+
+## What Contentful is for
+
+We use Contentful as the CMS for editorial content — homepage, banners, footer, campaign pages, and other marketing content.
+
+Commerce data (products, prices, orders) comes from SFCC.
+
+---
+
+## Concepts worth knowing upfront
+
+**Space** = the Zimmermann Contentful account. There is one shared space across all environments.
+
+**Environments** = isolated copies of the content schema and data within the space, e.g. `dev`, `test`, `master` (production). Your local dev server points at whichever environment is set in your `.env`.
+
+**Content type** = a schema (like a database table). Examples: `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`, etc. Defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed via `npm run sync:contentful`.
+
+**Experiences** — Contentful Studio's visual page-builder feature. An Experience is a page (e.g. the homepage) where an editor can drag and drop registered React components. Experiences are different to regular content entries — they have their own WYSIWYG editor in the Contentful UI.
+
+---
+
+## Setting up your local environment
+
+### 1. Get your personal management token
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your avatar (top right) → Account settings → [CMA tokens](app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens) → Create personal access token**. Give it a name like "My dev token" and set an expiry. Click **Generate**, then copy the token immediately — you will not see it again.
+
+Add it to your `.env` file (not `.env.sample`):
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=your-token-here
+```
+
+This token is personal — never commit or share it.
+
+### 2. Populate the rest of the Contentful env vars
+
+With your management token in `.env`, run:
+
+```bash
+npm run config:contentful
+```
+
+This fetches the delivery token, preview token, and environment ID from the live Contentful space and writes them into your `.env`. You only need to run this once (or again after rotating your management token).
+
+### 3. Point at the dev environment for local work
+
+After running `config:contentful`, check that your `.env` has:
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=dev
+```
+
+The default fetched value may be `master` (production). Switch it to `dev` for local development so you are not reading from or writing to live production content.
+
+---
+
+## Testing Contentful content locally
+
+When the local dev server is running (`npm start`), the PWA reads from the Contentful environment set in your `.env`.
+
+To connect Contentful's web editor to your local dev server so you can preview content changes live:
+
+1. Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Settings → Content preview → Create preview platform**.
+2. Fill in the fields:
+   - **Name:** something like "Zimmermann localhost"
+   - **Preview URL for Experiences:** `http://localhost:3000/{entry.fields.slug}`  
+     (To preview against the dev environment instead of localhost, use: `https://zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com/{entry.fields.slug}`)
+3. Go to **Experiences**, open an existing Experience (or create a new one).
+4. In the **Settings** tab on the left of the Experience editor, select the preview platform you just created (e.g. Zimmermann localhost).
+
+Changes you make in the Experience editor will now hot-reload in your browser.
+
+---
+
+## Browsing and creating content
+
+### Finding content types
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Content model**. This shows all available content types for Zimmermann (e.g. `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`).
+
+### Adding or changing a content type schema
+
+> **Don't confuse these two things:**
+>
+> - The `generate:contentful` script (and pre-commit hook) handles the **Experiences component registry** — it controls which React components appear in the Studio canvas. It only reads your source files; it never calls the Contentful API.
+> - `sync:contentful` (below) handles **content type schemas** — the field definitions pushed to the Contentful API. These are separate.
+>
+> A component like the test `ShoppableImage` has both: a content type schema (so editors can create ShoppableImage entries) and an Experiences registration (so it appears in the drag-and-drop canvas). They're maintained separately.
+
+**Content type schemas** are defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed to Contentful with:
+
+```bash
+npm run sync:contentful
+```
+
+This is for schema changes (adding/removing content type fields), not for creating content entries. It requires your `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Always run against a non-production environment first — the sync is additive-only and **cannot delete fields from a published content type**, so a mistaken field push to production is hard to undo.
+
+### Adding a content entry
+
+1. Go to **Content → Add entry** and pick a content type (e.g. PLP).
+2. Fill in the fields.
+3. Click **Publish**.
+
+The entry is now available via the Contentful Delivery API. On the PWA side, entries are queried by content type using the `useContentfulEntries` hook:
+
+```tsx
+import { useContentfulEntries } from '../../hooks/useContentful';
+
+// Fetches all entries of the 'plp' content type (e.g. hero banner, promo content)
+const { data, isLoading, error } = useContentfulEntries<PlpEntry>('plp');
+
+// data = PLP entries (if there are multiple) ordered by creation date
+const entry = data?.[0];
+```
+
+(Using that as an example because in PLP, the product list would come from SFCC, but editorial content (hero banner, promotional image/copy) comes from Contentful alongside it via this hook.)
+
+### Creating an Experience page
+
+Pages that are fully content-managed (like the home page and campaign/collection pages) use **Contentful Studio Experiences** (the WYSIWYG). The homepage is planned to be an Experience (the whole page laid out in Contentful Studio). While things like parts of the PLP, the footer, and the announcement banner/bar are regular content entries with editorial fields alongside their SFCC data.
+
+1. Go to **Experiences → Add experience**.
+2. Fill in:
+   - **Title:** your page name
+   - **Slug:** the URL path, e.g. `summer` makes the page live at `localhost:3000/summer` or `zimmermann.com/summer`
+3. Drag and drop registered components into the page canvas.
+4. Click **Publish** when ready.
+
+---
+
+## Registering a React component with Contentful
+
+To make a React component available in the Contentful Studio drag-and-drop canvas, it needs to be registered. Here is the full process:
+
+### 1. Place the component in the right folder
+
+Registerable components currently live in:
+
+```
+overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/
+```
+
+If you want to expose an existing component (e.g. `ProductCard`) to Contentful, create a thin wrapper in that folder rather than adding `@cf` tags to the original. The wrapper lets you deliberately limit which props editors can see and change them to be more editor-friendly, without touching the core component's interface:
+
+```tsx
+// overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/productCardCf.tsx
+import ProductCard from '../../productCard';
+
+type ProductCardCfProps = {
+  /** @cf Product ID */
+  productId: string;
+  /** @cf Show quick-add button, boolean */
+  showQuickAdd: boolean;
+};
+
+/** @cf-register */
+const ProductCardCf = ({ productId, showQuickAdd }: ProductCardCfProps) => (
+  <ProductCard id={productId} enableQuickAdd={showQuickAdd} />
+);
+
+export default ProductCardCf;
+```
+
+Internal props like `isLoading`, `onAddToCart`, or complex object shapes stay invisible to editors — only what you explicitly declare in the wrapper's `Props` type appears in the Contentful sidebar.
+
+### 2. Run the registration skill
+
+Run the `/contentful-register-component` Claude skill. It will:
+
+- Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before your component's `const` declaration — this opts it in to the code generator
+- Add `/** @cf Display Name */` JSDoc comments to each prop in your `Props` type — these tell Contentful what label and control to show in the editor sidebar
+
+### 3. The `@cf` tag syntax
+
+Each prop annotation follows this pattern:
+
+```ts
+type MyComponentProps = {
+  /** @cf Headline */
+  headline: string;
+
+  /** @cf Body Text, longText */
+  body: string;
+
+  /** @cf Layout, select */
+  imagePosition: 'left' | 'right';
+
+  /** @cf Background Image, media */
+  backgroundImage: ContentfulAsset;
+
+  /** @cf Show Border, boolean */
+  showBorder: boolean;
+};
+```
+
+- The first segment after `@cf` is the **display label** shown in the Contentful editor.
+- The second segment (optional) is the **control type** — a project-specific shorthand that the code generator translates into the correct Contentful field type internally (e.g. `string` → Contentful `Text`, `boolean` → Contentful `Boolean`, `media` → Contentful `Asset`). If omitted, the control is inferred from the TypeScript type.
+
+**Type-to-control inference:**
+
+| TypeScript type                     | Inferred control |
+| ----------------------------------- | ---------------- |
+| `string`                            | `string`         |
+| `boolean`                           | `boolean`        |
+| `number`                            | `number`         |
+| String literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select`         |
+

+# Contentful Developer Guide
+
+A draft guide for working with Contentful on the Zimmermann PWA.
+
+---
+
+## What Contentful is for
+
+We use Contentful as the CMS for editorial content — homepage, banners, footer, campaign pages, and other marketing content.
+
+Commerce data (products, prices, orders) comes from SFCC.
+
+---
+
+## Concepts worth knowing upfront
+
+**Space** = the Zimmermann Contentful account. There is one shared space across all environments.
+
+**Environments** = isolated copies of the content schema and data within the space, e.g. `dev`, `test`, `master` (production). Your local dev server points at whichever environment is set in your `.env`.
+
+**Content type** = a schema (like a database table). Examples: `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`, etc. Defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed via `npm run sync:contentful`.
+
+**Experiences** — Contentful Studio's visual page-builder feature. An Experience is a page (e.g. the homepage) where an editor can drag and drop registered React components. Experiences are different to regular content entries — they have their own WYSIWYG editor in the Contentful UI.
+
+---
+
+## Setting up your local environment
+
+### 1. Get your personal management token
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your avatar (top right) → Account settings → [CMA tokens](app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens) → Create personal access token**. Give it a name like "My dev token" and set an expiry. Click **Generate**, then copy the token immediately — you will not see it again.
+
+Add it to your `.env` file (not `.env.sample`):
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=your-token-here
+```
+
+This token is personal — never commit or share it.
+
+### 2. Populate the rest of the Contentful env vars
+
+With your management token in `.env`, run:
+
+```bash
+npm run config:contentful
+```
+
+This fetches the delivery token, preview token, and environment ID from the live Contentful space and writes them into your `.env`. You only need to run this once (or again after rotating your management token).
+
+### 3. Point at the dev environment for local work
+
+After running `config:contentful`, check that your `.env` has:
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=dev
+```
+
+The default fetched value may be `master` (production). Switch it to `dev` for local development so you are not reading from or writing to live production content.
+
+---
+
+## Testing Contentful content locally
+
+When the local dev server is running (`npm start`), the PWA reads from the Contentful environment set in your `.env`.
+
+To connect Contentful's web editor to your local dev server so you can preview content changes live:
+
+1. Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Settings → Content preview → Create preview platform**.
+2. Fill in the fields:
+   - **Name:** something like "Zimmermann localhost"
+   - **Preview URL for Experiences:** `http://localhost:3000/{entry.fields.slug}`  
+     (To preview against the dev environment instead of localhost, use: `https://zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com/{entry.fields.slug}`)
+3. Go to **Experiences**, open an existing Experience (or create a new one).
+4. In the **Settings** tab on the left of the Experience editor, select the preview platform you just created (e.g. Zimmermann localhost).
+
+Changes you make in the Experience editor will now hot-reload in your browser.
+
+---
+
+## Browsing and creating content
+
+### Finding content types
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Content model**. This shows all available content types for Zimmermann (e.g. `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`).
+
+### Adding or changing a content type schema
+
+> **Don't confuse these two things:**
+>
+> - The `generate:contentful` script (and pre-commit hook) handles the **Experiences component registry** — it controls which React components appear in the Studio canvas. It only reads your source files; it never calls the Contentful API.
+> - `sync:contentful` (below) handles **content type schemas** — the field definitions pushed to the Contentful API. These are separate.
+>
+> A component like the test `ShoppableImage` has both: a content type schema (so editors can create ShoppableImage entries) and an Experiences registration (so it appears in the drag-and-drop canvas). They're maintained separately.
+
+**Content type schemas** are defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed to Contentful with:
+
+```bash
+npm run sync:contentful
+```
+
+This is for schema changes (adding/removing content type fields), not for creating content entries. It requires your `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Always run against a non-production environment first — the sync is additive-only and **cannot delete fields from a published content type**, so a mistaken field push to production is hard to undo.
+
+### Adding a content entry
+
+1. Go to **Content → Add entry** and pick a content type (e.g. PLP).
+2. Fill in the fields.
+3. Click **Publish**.
+
+The entry is now available via the Contentful Delivery API. On the PWA side, entries are queried by content type using the `useContentfulEntries` hook:
+
+```tsx
+import { useContentfulEntries } from '../../hooks/useContentful';
+
+// Fetches all entries of the 'plp' content type (e.g. hero banner, promo content)
+const { data, isLoading, error } = useContentfulEntries<PlpEntry>('plp');
+
+// data = PLP entries (if there are multiple) ordered by creation date
+const entry = data?.[0];
+```
+
+(Using that as an example because in PLP, the product list would come from SFCC, but editorial content (hero banner, promotional image/copy) comes from Contentful alongside it via this hook.)
+
+### Creating an Experience page
+
+Pages that are fully content-managed (like the home page and campaign/collection pages) use **Contentful Studio Experiences** (the WYSIWYG). The homepage is planned to be an Experience (the whole page laid out in Contentful Studio). While things like parts of the PLP, the footer, and the announcement banner/bar are regular content entries with editorial fields alongside their SFCC data.
+
+1. Go to **Experiences → Add experience**.
+2. Fill in:
+   - **Title:** your page name
+   - **Slug:** the URL path, e.g. `summer` makes the page live at `localhost:3000/summer` or `zimmermann.com/summer`
+3. Drag and drop registered components into the page canvas.
+4. Click **Publish** when ready.
+
+---
+
+## Registering a React component with Contentful
+
+To make a React component available in the Contentful Studio drag-and-drop canvas, it needs to be registered. Here is the full process:
+
+### 1. Place the component in the right folder
+
+Registerable components currently live in:
+
+```
+overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/
+```
+
+If you want to expose an existing component (e.g. `ProductCard`) to Contentful, create a thin wrapper in that folder rather than adding `@cf` tags to the original. The wrapper lets you deliberately limit which props editors can see and change them to be more editor-friendly, without touching the core component's interface:
+
+```tsx
+// overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/productCardCf.tsx
+import ProductCard from '../../productCard';
+
+type ProductCardCfProps = {
+  /** @cf Product ID */
+  productId: string;
+  /** @cf Show quick-add button, boolean */
+  showQuickAdd: boolean;
+};
+
+/** @cf-register */
+const ProductCardCf = ({ productId, showQuickAdd }: ProductCardCfProps) => (
+  <ProductCard id={productId} enableQuickAdd={showQuickAdd} />
+);
+
+export default ProductCardCf;
+```
+
+Internal props like `isLoading`, `onAddToCart`, or complex object shapes stay invisible to editors — only what you explicitly declare in the wrapper's `Props` type appears in the Contentful sidebar.
+
+### 2. Run the registration skill
+
+Run the `/contentful-register-component` Claude skill. It will:
+
+- Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before your component's `const` declaration — this opts it in to the code generator
+- Add `/** @cf Display Name */` JSDoc comments to each prop in your `Props` type — these tell Contentful what label and control to show in the editor sidebar
+
+### 3. The `@cf` tag syntax
+
+Each prop annotation follows this pattern:
+
+```ts
+type MyComponentProps = {
+  /** @cf Headline */
+  headline: string;
+
+  /** @cf Body Text, longText */
+  body: string;
+
+  /** @cf Layout, select */
+  imagePosition: 'left' | 'right';
+
+  /** @cf Background Image, media */
+  backgroundImage: ContentfulAsset;
+
+  /** @cf Show Border, boolean */
+  showBorder: boolean;
+};
+```
+
+- The first segment after `@cf` is the **display label** shown in the Contentful editor.
+- The second segment (optional) is the **control type** — a project-specific shorthand that the code generator translates into the correct Contentful field type internally (e.g. `string` → Contentful `Text`, `boolean` → Contentful `Boolean`, `media` → Contentful `Asset`). If omitted, the control is inferred from the TypeScript type.
+
+**Type-to-control inference:**
+
+| TypeScript type                     | Inferred control |
+| ----------------------------------- | ---------------- |
+| `string`                            | `string`         |
+| `boolean`                           | `boolean`        |
+| `number`                            | `number`         |
+| String literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select`         |
+
+**Valid explicit controls:** `string`, `longText`, `select`, `boolean`, `number`, `media`
+
+Props beginning with `on` (event handlers) and `children` are skipped automatically.
+
+### 4. Generate the definitions file
+
+```bash
+npm run generate:contentful
+```
+
+This reads the `@cf-register` and `@cf` annotations and rewrites `definitions.ts` automatically. There is also a pre-commit hook that runs this whenever you stage a file from the `experiences/` folder.
+
+**Never edit `definitions.ts` by hand** — it is overwritten every time the generator runs.
+
+### 5. Verify
+
+```bash
+npx tsc --noEmit
+npm run generate:contentful:check
+```
+
+Once this passes, your component is immediately available in the Contentful Studio canvas. Open an Experience, open the component panel, and you should see it listed.

      "value": "Overview
--------

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,
banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery
API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 3 | TEST | `test` | `npm run push:test` | zimmermann-test.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com (to be created) |
| 4 | OMS INT | `sit` | `npm run push:sit` | zimmermann-sit.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 5 | STAGE | `staging` | `npm run push:staging` | zimmermann-stg.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |
| `it` | Italian | ZimmermannEUit | en |
| `es` | Spanish | ZimmermannEUes | en |
| `en-CH` | English (EU International) | ZimmermannEUIntl | en |
| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |
| **Current types** | shoppableImage | CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage |

### Migration format

jswide4000// scripts/contentful/migrations/002-my-change.mjs
export const id = '002-my-change';
export async function up(client, { environmentId }) {
// Use the contentful-management plain client
}

Drift Detection & Promotion Rules
---------------------------------

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

bashwide4000npm run detect:drift -- --source dev --target sit

| Script | Purpose | Who runs it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run setup:contentful` | Bootstrap environments, locales, API keys, and production alias | Tier 1 approver — once per space |
| `npm run config:contentful` | Populate .env with live API tokens from the space | Tier 1 approver (writes); any dev (read-only view) |
| `npm run sync:contentful` | Upsert content type definitions (dev environment only) | Any developer |

| `npm run promote:alias -- --target <env>` | Flip production + master aliases for a zero-downtime release | Tier 1 approver — per release |

===== FULL SKILL.md (check for OTHER stale shortText/toggle refs beyond the diff) =====
     1	---
     2	name: contentful-register-component
     3	description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
     4	allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Bash
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Contentful Component Registration
     8	
     9	Studio Experiences definitions are now **generated from code** — you never write a
    10	`defineComponents` entry by hand. The source of truth is the component's `Props` type,
    11	annotated with `@cf` JSDoc tags.
    12	
    13	## Steps
    14	
    15	### 1. Move the component into `experiences/`
    16	
    17	The codegen only processes files under
    18	`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. If the component isn't there yet,
    19	move it (or create it) in that folder.
    20	
    21	### 2. Add `/** @cf-register */` to the component
    22	
    23	Place it immediately before the component's `const` declaration:
    24	
    25	```tsx
    26	/** @cf-register */
    27	const MyComponent = ({ ... }: MyComponentProps) => { ... };
    28	
    29	export default MyComponent;
    30	```
    31	
    32	### 3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type
    33	
    34	Props without a `@cf` tag are silently skipped — omitting the tag is how you exclude a prop from the Contentful definition.
    35	
    36	```tsx
    37	type MyComponentProps = {
    38	  /** @cf Headline */
    39	  headline: string;
    40	
    41	  /** @cf Body Copy, longText */
    42	  body?: string;
    43	
    44	  /** @cf Hero Image, media */
    45	  heroImage?: string;
    46	
    47	  /** @cf Layout, select */
    48	  layout?: 'left' | 'right';
    49	
    50	  internalId?: string;
    51	};
    52	```
    53	
    54	**Tag syntax:**
    55	
    56	| Tag | Meaning |
    57	|-----|---------|
    58	| `/** @cf Display Name */` | Infer control from the TS type (see table below) |
    59	| `/** @cf Display Name, control */` | Override the inferred control |
    60	
    61	Props without any `@cf` tag are silently skipped — no tag needed to exclude a prop.
    62	
    63	**Type → control inference table:**
    64	
    65	| TypeScript type | Inferred control | Contentful variable type |
    66	|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
    67	| `string` | `shortText` | Text |
    68	| `boolean` | `toggle` | Boolean |
    69	| `number` | `number` | Number |
    70	| string literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select` | Text |
    71	
    72	**Valid explicit controls:** `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media`
    73	
    74	**Auto-skipped:** props starting with `on` (event handlers), `children` (emits
    75	`children: true` on the component registration instead), and any prop with no `@cf` tag.
    76	
    77	### 4. Run the generator
    78	
    79	```bash
    80	npm run generate:contentful
    81	```
    82	
    83	This rewrites `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`
    84	automatically. Verify the output looks correct, then commit both the annotated
    85	component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
    86	
    87	### 5. Verify
    88	
    89	```bash
    90	npx tsc --noEmit
    91	npm run generate:contentful:check
    92	```
    93	
    94	`--check` exits zero if `definitions.ts` is in sync with the source files.
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## Notes
    99	
   100	- **Never edit `definitions.ts` by hand** — it is autogenerated and will be overwritten
   101	  on the next run.
   102	- The pre-commit hook auto-runs the generator whenever an `experiences/*.tsx` file is
   103	  staged, so `definitions.ts` stays in sync automatically.
   104	- `children: ReactNode` → use `children: true` convention; the generator handles this
   105	  automatically when it sees a `children` prop.
   106	- `thumbnailUrl` is left blank until a real Contentful account exists.
   107	- Component `id` is auto-derived as kebab-case of the filename
   108	  (`myComponent.tsx` → `my-component`).
   109	- Component `name` is auto-derived as Title Case of the id words
   110	  (`my-component` → `My Component`).

Fair question — and the honest answer is that **the PR didn't change between the two passes; my depth of verification did.** Both passes ran against the exact same commit (`afc98857`). So the discrepancy is a gap in my first review, not new information or a moving target. Let me be specific about it.

## What each pass actually did

| | Pass 1 (go-signal) | Pass 2 (changes requested) |
|---|---|---|
| **Code rename** (`.mjs`, `SKILL.md`, `.mdc`) | Verified deeply (worktree byte-diff, sync check, Tier-1 check) | Re-confirmed — **same verdict: safe** |
| **The guide** (`humanContentfulGuide.md`) | *Spot-checked* — confirmed a few claims that happened to corroborate | **Traced its instructions into the actual scripts** |

The code verdict never changed. The entire difference is the guide, and it comes down to one thing:

**In Pass 1 I verified the guide's claims against sources that agreed with it. In Pass 2 I verified them against the code that would prove them wrong.**

## The specific gap

The guide's core instruction is: *"run `npm run config:contentful` — it writes the tokens into your `.env`."* To check that in Pass 1, I confirmed:
- the `config:contentful` script **exists** in `package.json` ✅
- the Confluence "Per-developer setup" blurb **says the same thing** ✅
- the referenced hooks/URLs exist ✅

All true — and all beside the point. I confirmed the command *exists*; I never opened [getConfig.mjs](scripts/contentful/setup/getConfig.mjs) to see what it *does*. When I did (Pass 2), it turned out writes are gated to tier-1-approvers and non-approvers get read-only — the opposite of what the guide promises.

Worse: the contradiction was **already inside evidence I had in Pass 1**. I read the Confluence "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" page — but I anchored on its friendly "Per-developer setup" paragraph and skimmed past its own **Scripts Reference table**, which plainly says config:contentful is *"Tier 1 approver (writes); any dev (read-only view)."* I even quoted that page approvingly. The fact was in front of me; I didn't reconcile the two halves of it.

## Why the second pass caught it

Two reasons, and I'll own both:

1. **The prompt reframed my job.** "The Tier-1 approvers are unsure" told me a competent reviewer already smelled something. That flipped me from *"confirm it's fine"* to *"find what's wrong"* — which is when I started tracing runnable instructions into their implementations instead of trusting corroboration. That's the correct posture, and I should have taken it the first time.

2. **I applied to the prose the same standard I'd applied to the code.** For the rename I insisted on executing it (the worktree diff) rather than reasoning about it. For the guide I initially reasoned instead of executing. A doc that tells developers to run commands has to be checked against those commands — the same rigor, just aimed at the prose.

## The bottom line

Pass 1's go-signal was **premature**, not a defensible alternate reading. Pass 2 is the correct verdict: code safe, guide needs fixing. Nothing about the PR justified the first "good for approval" — I just hadn't looked hard enough at the part where the risk actually lived.

The practical lesson, and how I'll treat the remaining PRs (39, 40): **for any doc/tooling PR, trace every "run this / it does X" claim into the actual script, and reconcile a reference page's *details* (tables, gates) against its *summaries* — don't let a corroborating sentence stand in for verifying behaviour.** If you want, I can re-run PR 38's guide claims line-by-line against the scripts to produce a definitive correction list, or carry this stricter bar straight into PR 39.

content.thinking:
The countries.ts file looks solid — it maintains business logic entries for all slugs in COUNTRY_OVERLAY, including 'en-ca', and validates that generated slugs have corresponding overlays. The COUNTRIES export then filters to only include overlays for countries that actually exist on the site, so 'en-ca' stays excluded until it's ready. For Hong Kong and Middle East, the checkout owner and global e-pricing settings align with the product requirements.

Now I'm realizing the currency field matters more than I initially thought — even though Global-e handles pricing and currency display downstream, SFCC still needs to send the cart in the correct currency (HKD for HK, AED for ME) to Global-e for proper processing. If the config incorrectly shows USD or EUR, that wrong currency could propagate through the checkout redirect logic and into the SFCC basket, causing a mismatch between what SFCC sends and what Global-e expects.

The complicating factor is that the dev BM sites are currently misconfigured with USD/EUR for HK/ME, so the generated config is actually reflecting the current broken state accurately — it's not lying about what's deployed, but it's committing a configuration that violates the PRD requirements. The real fix needs to happen upstream in BM, but if these generated files are resynced against production BM (which should have the correct currencies), the production deployment would get the right values, whereas the committed repo would still show the wrong ones.

Actually, wait — the generated files are static and committed once, not re-fetched per environment at runtime. So whatever currency values are committed from the dev sync would ship to all environments including production. If production BM has the correct HKD/AED but the committed file says USD/EUR, production would still use the wrong currencies. That's a latent production bug that strengthens the case for Finding B — this isn't just a dev lag issue, it's a committed configuration that violates the PRD and would break production unless the BM is fixed first and the files are re-synced before deployment.

Now I'm checking the contentfulMapping.generated.ts file to verify the locale configuration. The SUPPORTED_LOCALES array lists nine locales that match what's documented in Confluence, and the SITE_LOCALES mapping per PWA site also aligns with the overlay configuration. That checks out. Next I need to review the consumer code in contentfulMapping.ts and trace through the test fixtures and customer configuration to understand the full data flow.

Looking at the e2e fixtures, I'm seeing that both HK and ME regions have incorrect currency assignments—HK is set to USD instead of HKD, and ME is set to EUR instead of AED. This means any e2e tests validating these currencies would be testing against wrong values, since the fixtures themselves are derived from the same flawed data.

The customers.js fix expands the ADDRESSES map from a single `eu` key to region-specific keys (enEu, frEu, itEu, esEu, euIntl) plus hk and me, now matching the site.overlay.js structure. This is a solid fix for region-appropriate addresses, though I'm wondering if any existing tests referenced the old `eu` key that would now break—but the e2e job passed, so that's likely been handled.

contentfulMapping.ts is now re-exporting SUPPORTED_LOCALES and SITE_LOCALES from the generated file, which is a clean refactor. The type cast to SupportedLocale[] is a minor loosening of type safety but acceptable. Since it's not in the frozen or protected files lists, it's untiered and fine.

I need to check whether the BrowserStack E2E failure is actually caused by this PR, and also look at any CodeRabbit review comments the author mentioned addressing.

content.thinking:
I'm looking at the Confluence page that maps countries to their respective storefronts, which defines the routing logic for the eight storefronts: AU, Europe Domestic, Europe International, Hong Kong International, Middle East International, UK Domestic, US Domestic, and US International. This is the granular country-level selector data that determines which storefront each country routes to, and notably, PR #39 doesn't actually implement this mapping.

Instead, the PR sets up the storefront-level configuration (site, locale, currency per storefront) plus per-storefront overlays for shipping country, checkout owner, and boutique region. The country overlay in countries.ts is keyed by URL slug (au, us, uk, en-eu, etc.) — one entry per storefront rather than per country. So the full ~190-country mapping table that SFCC-49 specifically calls for isn't included in this PR, which means there's a gap between what SFCC-49 requires (the complete country list with each country mapped to its correct regional storefront) and what this PR delivers (the storefront-level foundation without the per-country routing table). The core issue is that SFCC-49 asks for a full ~190-country mapping for the country selector and address forms, but this PR only delivers per-storefront config with a handful of countries per storefront. It's a foundational piece, but it doesn't satisfy the ticket's actual acceptance criteria — so either this is an intentional first slice, or there's a scope gap worth flagging against the Jira requirements.

The country list also indirectly validates the currency setup: HK and ME are isolated storefronts with their own currencies (HKD and AED), which aligns with the regional docs. Australia appearing in multiple routing paths (Oceania default and Asia/Oceania via HK) is expected for the REG-027 use case, though the dual-AU routing itself is outside this PR's config scope.

I've checked the planning doc and README updates—both are minor and already addressed per CodeRabbit feedback. Now I'm verifying whether there's a TypeScript compilation check in the pipeline.

The PR modifies TypeScript files and adds generated ones, but the CI unit tests passed, which means compilation succeeded. The type casts and const assertions look fine, and the runtime throw for missing overlays is acceptable. I'm confident tsc passes given the CI results.

For the BrowserStack failure, I'm looking more closely at the error—it's the browserstack-node-sdk failing to find a config file, likely a `.browserstack` or similar configuration that the SDK expects.  This is happening at SDK initialization before any tests even run, which points to an infrastructure or environment issue rather than something caused by this PR's changes. The PR doesn't touch `.browserstack.yml`, the playwright config, or the CI workflow file, so this failure is almost certainly unrelated to the code changes—it's a tooling or working directory issue in the CI environment.

I should flag this as needing confirmation from the Integration/QA owner rather than treating it as a PR defect, especially since BrowserStack was skipped entirely on the previous PR (which was docs-only) and only ran here because there are code changes.

Now I'm ready to structure my full review: I'll lay out the PR summary, then highlight the two main findings—the governance issue with absolute file paths in `sites.js` and the correctness violation around Hong Kong and Middle East currency handling—followed by the technical quality assessment.

The verdict is clear: this cannot be approved as-is. The `sites.js` modification violates Hard Rule #4 (tier-1 exception doesn't apply), and the author's justification about Claude generating a snippet doesn't override the need for a documented governance decision from the Integration Lead. The currency PRD violation is the second blocker. The sync engine itself is solid—atomic writes, strict validation, proper gating—and the defaultLocale fix plus customers.js euIntl update are both correct; CodeRabbit's findings were addressed well. But this PR has a real governance problem and a data accuracy issue that undermine otherwise strong technical work, so I need to be fair but clear about what needs fixing before merge. The author themselves admits config/sites.js is on the absolute list, then argues that having Claude produce the snippet and a human apply it circumvents the rule — but that's exactly the kind of workaround that defeats the control's intent. The author even frames it as "it just can't see who actually typed the change," which shows they understand they're sidestepping the guideline, and that's precisely what shouldn't pass review.

This is a real governance breach, though likely good-faith. I should present the findings clearly and fairly without assuming malice, but the process violation and invalid justification are solid. Now I'll write a structured verdict with proper file references.

I now have an exhaustive, evidence-backed picture. The Confluence "Country List per Storefront" page (which SFCC-49 cites) is the ~190-country → storefront routing table — and notably this PR delivers **storefront-level** config, not that per-country list, which bears on SFCC-49 scope. Here is the verdict.

---

# 📋 Deep Code Review — PR #39: `feat(sfcc): sync regional site/locale/currency config from live SCAPI data`

**Author:** TimLavelleACC (tier-1-approver) · **Branch:** `feature/SFCC-49-storefront-config` → `develop` · **+1176 / −350**, 16 files · **State:** OPEN, `BLOCKED` / `REVIEW_REQUIRED`
[PR #39](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/39) · Jira: [SFCC-49 "Country List Configuration"](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-49) (Epic SFCC-19, status **Tech design**)

## What it does
Adds `npm run sync:regional-config` ([syncRegionalConfig.mjs](scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs) + [_shared.mjs](scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs)) that pulls live site/locale/currency data from SCAPI Shopper Configurations and regenerates four `*.generated.*` files, each merged by a hand-maintained overlay. Replaces four independently hand-maintained files with one sync path. Fixes an e2e fixture gap and a `defaultLocale` bug.

## The engineering is genuinely strong ✅
- **Sync engine:** atomic four-file publish (temp + `eslint --fix` per target, rename-all-or-nothing with cleanup), fatal-on-malformed-response (aborts the whole run rather than silently dropping a region), fail-closed tier-1 write gate, 20s bounded timeouts. All 8 substantive CodeRabbit findings were properly fixed in `067857f`.
- **Merge logic:** [config/sites.js](config/sites.js) and [countries.ts](overrides/app/config/countries.ts) throw loudly on overlay/generated mismatches; `en-ca` (US-intl, TBC) is correctly carried in the overlay but excluded until its site exists.
- **The `defaultLocale` fix is real and correct** — using the overlay's own locale instead of SCAPI's shared site-level default (which would crash `AppConfig.restore` for AU and mis-default 3 EU sites). Well reasoned.
- **`customers.js` fix** (10 keys, `euIntl` added) is a legitimate pre-existing-bug fix.

But two issues make this **not approvable as-is**, plus supporting concerns.

---

## 🔴 Blocker 1 — Governance: `config/sites.js` is an *absolute* frozen file; the stated exception does not apply

[config/sites.js](config/sites.js) is **modified** (+49/−169). Per **AGENTS.md Hard Rule #4**, it is one of four *absolute* files where *"the verified-session exception … does not apply to them, **regardless of approver status**."*

The author resolved CodeRabbit's Major "config/ is expressly prohibited" finding with this rebuttal (thread now marked resolved):

> *"I (Claude) never edited this file… written by me as a snippet and applied by @TimLavelleACC by hand… the guideline is working as intended, it just can't see who actually typed the change."*

This does **not** hold up:
- It's a **letter-vs-spirit evasion.** The rule's intent is that this file must not change through the AI-assisted workflow at all — the *"regardless of approver status"* clause deliberately removes the tier-1 escape hatch precisely so a verified approver *can't* wave it through. "Claude dictates it, a verified approver pastes it" defeats that intent while satisfying only the literal tool restriction — the author's own phrasing ("it just can't see who actually typed the change") concedes the control was *evaded*, not *met*.
- Calling it *"the approved exception working as intended"* is **factually wrong** — there is no approved exception for `config/sites.js`; the author's own reply even acknowledges the file is on the absolute list.

**Important distinction — the new files are fine.** [config/sites.overlay.js](config/sites.overlay.js) and [config/sites.generated.js](config/sites.generated.js) are Tier 1 (whole-`config/` rule) but **not** on the absolute list, so the verified-tier-1-approver exception legitimately applies there. The author's handling of *those* is correct. The problem is isolated to the modification of `config/sites.js` itself.

**What this needs:** a conscious, documented decision by the `config/` owner (**Integration Lead, #integration**) — either an explicit accepted exception acknowledging Hard Rule #4, or an amendment to Hard Rule #4 if the team wants to permit this refactor pattern. It should **not** be self-approved by a tier-1-approver on the current (incorrect) justification. Note the CI "🔴 Tier 1 Frozen Files Check" passing is meaningless here — it's [informational-only by design](.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml) and `config/**` *is* on its watch list.

## 🔴 Blocker 2 — Correctness: committed HK/ME currencies violate the PRD

[config/sites.generated.js](config/sites.generated.js), [countries.generated.ts](overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts), and [e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js](e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js) all commit:
- **HK → `USD`** (should be **HKD**)
- **ME → `EUR`** (should be **AED**)

This directly violates **regional.md §1 (REG-007 / REG-008)**, which mandates HK=HKD and ME=AED ("SFCC price books"), and is corroborated by the Confluence country-list source. The author attributes it to "sandbox-configuration lag" — but:
- The **generated files are committed static**, not re-fetched per environment, so these values ship to **prod**, feeding `COUNTRIES` (which drives "URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic" per the file header) and the SFCC basket currency sent to Global-e.
- The sync **has no currency/locale validation** ([syncRegionalConfig.mjs:128-136](scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs) assigns `defaultCurrency` verbatim), so wrong upstream data is committed silently. Here's the precise, itemised breakdown of every defect I've verified in each PR — with exact locations, what's wrong, and why.

---

# PR #38 — "Draft Contentful developer guide"

> The code rename (`shortText→string`, `toggle→boolean` across `generateDefinitions.mjs`, `SKILL.md`, `.mdc`) is **correct and safe** — verified output-neutral. **Every defect below is in the new guide**, [.docs/temp/humanContentfulGuide.md](.docs/temp/humanContentfulGuide.md).

### 🟠 38.1 — The core setup instruction is false for most developers
**Where:** guide §2 "Populate the rest of the Contentful env vars"
**Says:** *"run `npm run config:contentful`. This fetches the delivery token, preview token, and environment ID from the live Contentful space and writes them into your `.env`. You only need to run this once."*
**Why it's wrong:** [getConfig.mjs:11](scripts/contentful/setup/getConfig.mjs) — *"Write access (add/update) is gated to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. Non-approvers get a read-only view."* The end of `main()` returns without writing for non-approvers (`if (!canWrite) { … 'Read-only — contact a tier-1-approver' … return }`), and the read-only output **masks** the tokens (`deliveryToken.slice(0,8)…`). So a normal developer running this gets nothing written and can't even copy the values. Their Contentful setup silently fails.

### 🟠 38.2 — Omits the project's actual onboarding path
**Where:** guide §1–§3
**Says:** hand-edit `.env` with `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=…`, then run `config:contentful`.
**Why it's wrong:** [.env.sample](.env.sample) header documents the real flow: token goes in **`.env.shared`** (it's `scope:personal`), then `npm run env -- init`, which pulls per-tier Contentful tokens from GitHub Environments. The guide never mentions `npm run env`, `.env.shared`, or the tier system. It also contradicts the canonical Confluence page's Scripts Reference (*"config:contentful … Tier 1 approver (writes); any dev (read-only view)"*).

### 🟡 38.3 — Unstated prerequisite
**Where:** guide §2
**Why it's wrong:** [getConfig.mjs:41](scripts/contentful/setup/getConfig.mjs) `checkEnv(['CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN', 'CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID'])` — it **requires `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` already present**, which the guide never mentions (it only reaches `.env` via `npm run env`).

### 🟡 38.4 — Mis-attributes a behaviour
**Where:** guide §2 ("…and environment ID…and writes them") and §3 ("The default fetched value may be `master`")
**Why it's wrong:** `getConfig.mjs` never upserts `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` (it only writes SPACE_ID / DELIVERY_TOKEN / PREVIEW_TOKEN). The `master` default comes from [.env.sample:117](.env.sample), not from config:contentful "fetching" it.

### ⚪ 38.5 — Pre-existing, not introduced (FYI only)
[generateDefinitions.mjs:11](scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs) references `.docs/temp/contentfulCodegen.md` for the "full spec" — that file doesn't exist. Not this PR's fault, but this PR is the natural place to fix it.

**Net:** merge the rename; the guide's §1–§3 need correcting first (or trim them and link to Confluence).

---

# PR #39 — "sync regional site/locale/currency config"

> The sync engine is well-built. The defects are one **confirmed data bug** and one **contested governance call**.

### 🔴 39.1 — Committed HK/ME currencies violate the PRD and ship to production
**Where — the wrong values are committed in three files:**
- [config/sites.generated.js](config/sites.generated.js): `ZimmermannHK` → `defaultCurrency: 'USD'`, `supportedCurrencies: ['USD']` (lines ~103-106); `ZimmermannME` → `'EUR'` (lines ~119-122)
- [countries.generated.ts](overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts): `hk … currency: 'USD'` (line 17); `'en-ae' … currency: 'EUR'` (line 18)
- [e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js](e2e/fixtures/site.generated.js): `hk … 'USD'` (line 17); `me … 'EUR'` (line 18)

**Why it's wrong:** [regional.md §1](.docs/prd/regional.md) is explicit — **HK = HKD (REG-007), ME = AED (REG-008)**, "SFCC price books." The author's own PR body concedes: *"dev realm currently returns HK: USD/ME: EUR instead of the documented HKD/AED targets."*
**Why it matters (verified):** there is **no `sync:regional-config` step in any build or deploy workflow** — `push:prod` just runs `pwa-kit-dev build && push`, so the committed generated files bundle **as-is into prod**. `countries.ts` feeds "URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic," and the wrong `supportedCurrencies` sets the SFCC basket currency sent to Global-e. Regional Storefront is **active work this sprint** ([sprintScope](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md), Sprint 2), so this is being laid into the live foundation.

### 🟠 39.2 — The sync has no currency guard, so wrong data commits silently
**Where:** [syncRegionalConfig.mjs:128-136](scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs) — `defaultCurrency = fields.defaultCurrency` and every locale gets `preferredCurrency: defaultCurrency`, verbatim from BM.
**Why it's wrong:** there's no assertion that fetched currency matches the PRD-documented value, so a misconfigured BM (like now) ships wrong data with no signal. The e2e fixture carries the *same* wrong value, so any currency test passes against the wrong number — masking it.

### 🟡 39.3 — Misleading test-plan checkbox
**Where:** PR body Test plan
**Why it's wrong:** the item *"Re-run `sync:regional-config` once BM's HK/ME currencies are corrected"* is marked `[x]` (done), but the committed files still show USD/EUR — it demonstrably wasn't done.

### 🟠 39.4 — Modifies `config/sites.js` (absolute file) — contested governance
**Where:** [config/sites.js](config/sites.js) modified (+49/−169); [AGENTS.md:33](AGENTS.md) Hard Rule #4 names it *absolute*, exception *"does not apply … regardless of approver status."*
**What's actually wrong (precisely):** the author's PR-thread justification — *"the approved exception working as intended"* — **is incorrect**: there is no approved exception for `config/sites.js`. The "Claude wrote a snippet, a human pasted it" workaround honours the letter of a Claude-behaviour rule but is a **genuine gray area** on the spirit. This is **not a clear defect** — it's a call that must be **adjudicated by the config/ owner (Integration Lead)**, not self-certified. (The new files `sites.overlay.js` / `sites.generated.js` are fine — Tier 1 but not absolute, so the exception legitimately applies.)

### 🟡 39.5 — SFCC-49 not fully delivered
**Where:** [countries.ts](overrides/app/config/countries.ts) `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE` / `COUNTRY_OVERLAY` — ~10 entries (one per storefront).
**Why it's wrong:** [SFCC-49](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-49) is the **full ~190-country → storefront map** (per its Confluence "Country List per Storefront"), for the country selector/address forms. This PR delivers storefront-level config, not that list — so the ticket is (at best) partially satisfied.

### ⚪ 39.6 — BrowserStack red (likely environmental, confirm)
The check fails at **SDK init** (`"Config file does not exist"` + yargs crash in `browserstack-node-sdk`), before any test runs. This PR touches no BrowserStack/Playwright config, so it looks like a tooling/secrets issue, **not** a test-logic failure from this PR — but it's red and should be confirmed with the QA/Integration owner.

**Net:** blocked on 39.1 (fix BM + re-sync + add 39.2 guard); 39.4 needs Integration-Lead adjudication.

---

# PR #40 — "CodeRabbit CLI skill, reply discipline, onboarding"

> Mechanically the cleanest PR. Defects are a doc contradiction, governance scope, and a few judgment calls.

### 🟠 40.1 — Self-contradiction the PR introduces: "required" vs "optional"
**Where:** [.env.sample:296-299](.env.sample) still says *"Optional — the CLI step is skipped with a note if this is blank or the CLI isn't installed."*
**Why it's wrong:** this PR changes [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) step 4, [README.md](README.md), and [onboarding SKILL.md](.claude/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md) to *"**required, not optional** … stop and have the developer install it."* The new AGENTS.md text even points to `.env.sample`, which now flatly contradicts it. `.env.sample` wasn't updated in the PR.

### 🟠 40.2 — Vendored skill conflicts with the mandatory workflow
**Where:** [.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md) §4 "Fix Issues (Autonomous Workflow)" — *"Implement the requested feature → run review → fix critical/warning → repeat until clean."*
**Why it's wrong:** that directly contradicts AGENTS.md's mandatory clarify → plan → **pause for confirmation** workflow and Hard Rule #12 (one question at a time, no autonomous multi-step). It's hash-pinned so shouldn't be hand-patched — but the conflict is resolved only by asserting "instruction precedence," which relies on every session correctly choosing AGENTS.md over an active skill's explicit instructions.

### 🟡 40.3 — "Required" is unenforced + has a rollout dependency
**Where:** [.env.sample:301](.env.sample) `CODERABBIT_API_KEY=` (blank; `scope:shared`; needs a tier-1-approver to generate + `npm run env -- push shared`).
**Why it's wrong:** no hook actually runs the CLI, so "required" is honour-system. And if the shared key isn't published yet, the new "stop if missing" policy could block the whole team.

### 🟡 40.4 — New skill missing from the inventory; safeguard bypassed
**Where:** `.claude/skills/README.md` and the mirrored Confluence "Skills Reference" — **not updated** for the new `code-review` skill.
**Why it's wrong:** because the skill is vendored under `.agents/` and symlinked, the staged paths don't match the pre-commit **1c inventory-reminder** regex (`^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$`), so that safeguard silently didn't fire.

### 🟡 40.5 — Bot review not cleared
CodeRabbit's latest review is **`CHANGES_REQUESTED`** (it didn't flip to approved as on #39). The `pre-commit:225` "blanket bypass when any AI source is staged" Major finding was *declined* (defensibly — step 1b regenerates-and-restages first, so it's safe) but **not withdrawn** by the bot.

### 🔵 40.6 — Governance scope (the decisive one)
**Where:** AGENTS.md footer — *"changes require both squad leads and the Integration lead."*
**Why it matters:** the AGENTS.md edits (required-CLI policy + reply discipline) **cannot be a solo tier-1 approval** — they need all three owners.

### ⚪ 40.7 — Cross-PR risk (raised for owners)
The new reply-discipline rule + CodeRabbit's learning loop means a confident-but-wrong justification (e.g. #39's "approved exception") can **train CodeRabbit to stop flagging** legitimate Tier-1/absolute-file issues. Worth a caveat: dismissing a Tier-1/absolute finding needs human sign-off, not just an in-thread reply.

**Net:** fix 40.1; route the AGENTS.md changes through 3-owner sign-off (40.6) and confirm the key is published (40.3).
